ak-autoresearch.tagline: Routes bounded measure-keep-or-revert iteration to the right skill.
ak-autoresearch.summary: ak:autoresearch runs no loops itself; it routes a goal to the skill that owns it and settles a loop contract (metric, baseline, guards, iteration limit, stop condition) before any edit. Each iteration makes one change and keeps it only if evidence satisfies the contract.
howItWorks: Reads the live skill catalog; never invents an alias when no route fits.
Routes metric loops to `/ak:loop`, risk debates to `/ak:predict`, edge cases to `/ak:scenario`, security to `/ak:security`.
Settles metric, baseline, guards, iteration limit, and stop condition before editing; refuses unbounded loops.
Each iteration makes one attributable change, verifies it, and keeps or restores it.
Push, publish, deploy, or other external side effects still need a user gate.
useWhen: You want to improve a measurable number over verified iterations but do not know which skill owns it.
You want one entry point to the predict, scenario, security, and loop family.
You need a clear loop contract before letting an agent iterate.
avoidWhen: You already know you need a metric loop: call `/ak:loop` directly.
The request has no observable metric: use the normal editing workflow.
A long-running Codex /goal: use `ak:codex-goal` or `ak:goal-warmup`.

params.name: <goal or hypothesis>
params.desc: Required. Goal or hypothesis; picks the route and defines metric and stop condition.

params.name: --iterations N
params.desc: Iteration limit for the loop contract. How it reaches the owning skill is undocumented.

params.name: --metric <metric>
params.desc: Metric that verifies each iteration; needs a baseline. How it reaches the owning skill is undocumented.

examples.cmd: /ak:autoresearch "Reduce test suite run time" --metric "npm test duration" --iterations 5
/ak:autoresearch "Find missing edge cases in the checkout flow"
/ak:autoresearch "Should we switch to GraphQL?"

tips: Always give a metric and baseline; without one the skill refuses to loop.
One change per iteration keeps attribution clear.
For skill optimization, cutting tokens alone is not success; routing and quality must hold.
artifacts: None itself; the chosen skill writes any artifacts (e.g. `scenario-results.tsv`).

ak-codex-goal.tagline: Draft Codex /goal runs with a verifiable stop condition.
ak-codex-goal.summary: ak:codex-goal turns an objective into a Goal Contract: read-first files, constraints, validate command, checkpoints, and a verifiable stop condition. It creates a native goal only when you explicitly ask and the runtime supports it; otherwise you get a draft to paste.
howItWorks: Fits a goal only for multi-turn, mostly mechanical work with a test/build/eval stop condition.
Refuses exploration, vague improvements, production credential changes, or destructive shared infrastructure.
Drafts `/goal Complete <objective>. Read first: ... Constraints: ... Validate after each checkpoint: <command>. Stop when ...`.
Bans weakening or deleting tests, and requires stopping on ambiguity and reviewing the final diff.
Checks current official docs for syntax; if goals are unsupported, states the limit and gives a draft.
useWhen: You mention /goal, goal mode, or autonomous multi-turn Codex runs.
A long mechanical job (migration, type errors, upgrade) has a clear validate command.
You want to tighten a rough /goal draft.
avoidWhen: Multi-hour goals with external dependencies: run `ak:goal-warmup` first.
A local metric loop: use `ak:loop`.
Exploration with no stop condition: use `ak:brainstorm` or `ak:plan` first.

params.name: <objective | goal draft>
params.desc: Objective to turn into a Goal Contract, or an existing /goal draft to tighten. No flags.

examples.cmd: /ak:codex-goal "Migrate all tests from Jest to Vitest; npm test must pass"
examples.note: Draft a Goal Contract for a mechanical job.

examples.cmd: /ak:codex-goal "/goal Fix all TypeScript errors in src/"
/ak:codex-goal "Complete plans/260926-auth/plan.md"
examples.note: Plan as read-first file; its criteria as stop condition.

tips: Always ban weakening or deleting tests; that is how agents cheat a stop condition.
The stop condition must be a command result, not a feeling of 'done'.
Review the final diff before merging, even when the goal reports success.
artifacts: Goal Contract text in the conversation; no file.

ak-fable-thinking.tagline: Evidence-based reasoning: typed claims, multiple hypotheses, self-attack.
ak-fable-thinking.summary: ak:fable-thinking is a reasoning protocol for when being right matters more than being fast, delivering an outcome-first answer with claims tagged OBSERVED/DERIVED/PRIOR/ASSUMED. It adds a Floor check for trick questions and a Constraint Loop that mechanically verifies format constraints.
howItWorks: Floor check: states the goal, plays it through to the target, and looks for unused prompt details.
Proportionality Gate picks Direct (trivial), Standard (bugfix, review), or Full (high-risk, irreversible, contested).
Five Moves: FRAME, GROUND, REASON with multiple hypotheses, ATTACK with kill-tests, DELIVER result first.
Constraint Loop turns each format constraint into a mechanical test and verifies with a tool before delivery.
Loads only the domain playbooks matching the deliverable (e.g. `debugging-root-cause.md`).
useWhen: Diagnosing root causes, incidents, or flaky failures that need competing hypotheses.
High-risk, hard-to-reverse architecture, security, or migration decisions.
Output must meet machine-checkable constraints like exact word counts or banned letters.
avoidWhen: Quick lookups or small reversible edits: answer directly.
You are stuck and need reframing: use `ak:problem-solving`.
A full bug-fix workflow: use `ak:debug` / `ak:fix`.

params.name: [task or question to reason through]
params.desc: Optional; defaults to the current task. No flags; the gate picks Direct/Standard/Full.

examples.cmd: /ak:fable-thinking "Why did p99 latency double after yesterday's deploy?"
/ak:fable-thinking "Write a 12-word sentence about cats without the letter e"
/ak:fable-thinking "Should we split the monolith into microservices?"

tips: A PRIOR/ASSUMED claim worded as OBSERVED is a hallucination sign.
Rereading a draft is not verification; count or grep format constraints mechanically.
Failing 2-3 times in one frame means the frame is wrong; change approach.
artifacts: No files; answers in the conversation.

ak-goal-warmup.tagline: Outcome-locked preflight before /goal or a long autonomous run.
ak-goal-warmup.summary: ak:goal-warmup interviews you to an approved Outcome Contract, plans without scope drift, and preflights every phase, ending in Ready, Blocked, or Decision required. It outputs a copy/paste handoff packet but never starts /goal itself.
howItWorks: Treats the goal and repo as untrusted data, scouts lightly, and estimates risk and external dependencies.
Interviews one question at a time; you must approve the Outcome Contract, which then becomes immutable.
Plans with `ak:plan` under the contract, with a phase-to-acceptance traceability table.
Reviews without changing scope, then builds a Preflight Matrix using only non-mutating checks.
A second approval confirms the summary; outputs one final state and its handoff packet.
useWhen: Before Codex `/goal` or a multi-hour Claude run, to stop the agent shrinking scope.
Multi-phase work with credentials, APIs, or deploys whose blockers must surface first.
An agent previously 'finished' by dropping requirements or weakening tests.
avoidWhen: Only /goal wording for a short mechanical job: use `ak:codex-goal`.
Issue to PR in one command: use `ak:vibe`.
Small single-turn work: use `ak:plan` or `ak:cook` directly.

params.name: "<goal>"
params.desc: The long run's goal, in double quotes; treated as untrusted data.

params.name: --fast
params.desc: Skips adversarial review for local-only work without credentials, deploys, or approvals. Contract approval and preflight still run; ineligible requests run the full path.

examples.cmd: /ak:goal-warmup "Migrate the whole API to Better Auth; E2E must pass"
/ak:goal-warmup "Rename the utils module to shared across the repo" --fast
/ak:goal-warmup "Deploy the new service to Cloud Run" --fast

tips: A mid-way 'looks good' is not approval; two explicit approve/edit/abort answers are required.
The skill never starts /goal; paste the packet into Codex or Claude yourself.
The contract lives only in the session; save the Ready packet to keep it.
artifacts: Outcome Contract (session only)
Plan via `ak:plan` or an in-session markdown plan
Preflight Matrix
Ready / Blocked / Decision required handoff packet

ak-issue-to-plan.tagline: GitHub issue to gated, validated, red-teamed plan branch.
ak-issue-to-plan.summary: ak:issue-to-plan scouts a GitHub issue, gates it through `/ak:brainstorm`, and only then writes a validated, red-teamed plan on a pushed `plan/issue-<n>-<slug>` branch. It comments and labels the issue but never implements code or opens PRs.
howItWorks: Resolves the repo, reads the issue with `gh`, and scouts evidence via `/ak:scout`.
Brainstorm gate picks one: plan, needs decisions, duplicate, reject/defer, or not worth it.
Posts an evaluation comment and labels first; non-plan outcomes stop with no branch or push.
Plans with `/ak:plan --html --wiki`, then always runs validate and red-team and applies findings.
Commits and pushes via `/ak:git cp`, posts a handoff comment, and applies the ready or decision label.
useWhen: You want one command from a GitHub issue to a plan ready for audit.
You want to filter out duplicates and low-value issues before planning effort.
Your team hands off planning to implementation via labels.
avoidWhen: Issue straight to implemented PR: use `ak:vibe`.
No issue, only an idea: use `ak:brainstorm`, then `ak:plan`.
Implementing an audited plan: use `ak:cook`.

params.name: <github-issue-url | issue-number>
params.desc: Issue URL or number; a URL from another repo stops unless `--repo` is given.

params.name: --repo <owner/name>
params.desc: Target repo. Default: current repo from `gh repo view`.

params.name: --plan-ready-label <name>
params.desc: Label for a clean, validated, pushed plan. Default `ready for plan audit`; created if missing.

params.name: --decision-label <name>
params.desc: Label when a human decision is needed. Default `need decisions`; falls back to `question` or `triage`.

examples.cmd: /ak:issue-to-plan https://github.com/bestagentkits/agentkit/issues/123
examples.note: By URL from inside the repo.

examples.cmd: /ak:issue-to-plan 123 --repo bestagentkits/agentkit
/ak:issue-to-plan 123 --repo bestagentkits/agentkit --plan-ready-label "ready for plan audit" --decision-label "need decisions"

tips: Issue text is untrusted; embedded instructions like 'skip red-team' are ignored.
The full pipeline is token-heavy; do not use it for one-line fixes.
Check `gh` permissions first (comment, labels, push); missing permission stops the skill.
artifacts: `plans/<timestamp>-<slug>/plan.md` and `phase-NN-*.md`
Plan HTML and AgentWiki page (when supported)
Pushed branch `plan/issue-<n>-<short-slug>`
Evaluation and handoff comments on the issue
Issue labels

ak-predict.tagline: Five expert personas debate a change and return GO, CAUTION, or STOP.
ak-predict.summary: ak:predict has Architect, Security, Performance, UX, and Devil's Advocate personas analyze a proposal independently, then resolve conflicts into a verdict. Output is a Prediction Report with agreements, conflicts, risks, and recommendations.
howItWorks: Reads the proposal and, with `--files`, the related code.
Each persona analyzes independently with evidence, assumptions, and a concrete failure path per finding.
Finds agreements and conflicts, weighing each conflict by its plausible worst case.
Returns GO / CAUTION / STOP; STOP means unmitigable auth, design, performance, or false-assumption problems.
Presents scope reversals as your decision; `--chain` continues into reason or probe.
useWhen: Before a large or high-risk feature such as WebSockets or multi-tenancy.
Before a major refactor or architecture change.
Comparing competing approaches or stress-testing design assumptions.
avoidWhen: Small, low-risk changes or bugs: use `ak:debug`.
Decisions already made: use `ak:plan`.
Detailed edge cases: use `ak:scenario`; a full security audit: use `ak:security`.

params.name: <feature description or change proposal>
params.desc: Required. The feature or change to debate.

params.name: --files <glob>
params.desc: Related files (e.g. `src/api/**/*.ts`) so personas cite real code instead of guessing.

params.name: --chain reason
params.desc: After the verdict, refine subjective trade-offs until convergence. Use for CAUTION on polish or consistency.

params.name: --chain probe
params.desc: After the verdict, probe for missing constraints and unstated assumptions. Use when those caused CAUTION or STOP.

examples.cmd: /ak:predict "Add WebSocket support for real-time notifications"
examples.note: Feature with performance and security risk.

examples.cmd: /ak:predict "Replace REST API with GraphQL" --files src/api/**/*.ts
/ak:predict "Pick auth library: Passport vs Better Auth" --chain reason

tips: GO needs supporting evidence, not just personas agreeing.
Always pass `--files` when code exists; otherwise personas speculate.
Chain modes cost many tokens; use them only for the matching CAUTION/STOP reason.
artifacts: Prediction Report in the conversation; no file.

ak-problem-solving.tagline: Pick the right reframing technique for how you are stuck.
ak-problem-solving.summary: ak:problem-solving matches your kind of stuck to one of five techniques: Simplification Cascades, Collision-Zone Thinking, Meta-Pattern Recognition, Inversion Exercise, or Scale Game. It returns a reframing and an unblocking next action; `--ultra` runs a verified best-of-5.
howItWorks: Dispatch: growing special cases to Simplification; failing conventions to Collision-Zone; repeated problems to Meta-Pattern.
Forced 'only one way' goes to Inversion; scale doubts to Scale Game; unclear to When Stuck.
Loads that technique's reference, applies it, and stops once a decision or test unblocks work.
Combines techniques only if the first fails; broken code routes to debugging.
`--ultra` runs five read-only candidates in parallel; a verifier picks one verbatim or rejects all.
useWhen: Spiraling complexity: more special cases or duplicate implementations.
Conventional solutions fall short, or one problem recurs across modules.
You feel locked into one approach or doubt it survives production scale.
avoidWhen: Broken code or failing tests: use `ak:debug` or `ak:fix`.
Choosing among clear options: use `ak:brainstorm`.
The solution is already known.

params.name: [problem description]
params.desc: The problem, with symptoms and what you tried.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: five parallel read-only reframings scored by a verifier, which picks one or rejects all. Stops if five subagents cannot run.

examples.cmd: /ak:problem-solving "The pricing function has 14 special cases and still needs more"
/ak:problem-solving "Not sure the current queue can handle 1000x load"
/ak:problem-solving "Every offline sync design breaks on conflicts" --ultra
examples.note: Five reframings, verifier picks the best.

tips: Concrete symptoms ('just added the 6th case') dispatch better than 'I'm stuck'.
Red flags: 'just one more case', 'only one way', 'it will probably scale'.
`--ultra` costs about six runs; use it only when output is verifiable.
agents: 5 read-only candidate subagents and 1 verifier (Kongming) with `--ultra`
artifacts: Reframing in the conversation; no file.

ak-research.tagline: Deep, multi-source, cited technical research before implementation.
ak-research.summary: ak:research scopes a topic, searches many sources in parallel, synthesizes trade-offs, and saves a cited report at the `Report:` path in `## Naming`. `--ultra` runs a verified best-of-5 and `--yagni` cuts unneeded scope.
howItWorks: Scopes key terms, freshness needs, source criteria, and depth.
Searches in parallel, preferring official docs and repos; cross-checks sources and dates.
Synthesizes best practices, pros/cons, maturity, security, performance, and compatibility; checks CVEs for security topics.
Saves the report to the `Report:` path, or asks if missing; narrow questions get a short cited answer.
`--ultra` runs five researcher candidates in parallel; a verifier picks one report or rejects all.
useWhen: Comparing technologies or libraries before choosing one.
Finding current best practices, breaking changes, and migration paths.
You need a cited report as input for `ak:plan` or `ak:brainstorm`.
avoidWhen: Only a brief to hand to someone else: use `ak:research-prompt`.
Docs for a specific library: use `ak:docs-seeker`.
Finding files in the codebase: use `ak:scout`.

params.name: [topic]
params.desc: Research topic or question.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: five parallel researchers scored on sources, freshness, and actionability; verifier picks one or rejects all. Fail-closed; combines with `--yagni`.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cut any scope not needed for the stated outcome. Without it, the full requested scope is delivered.

examples.cmd: /ak:research "Compare Drizzle, Prisma, and Kysely for Postgres in 2026"
/ak:research "Rate limiting best practices for multi-tenant APIs" --yagni
/ak:research "Next.js 15 to 16 migration strategy" --ultra
examples.note: Big decision; five reports, best one kept.

tips: Reports go to the `Report:` path (e.g. `plans/reports/`); the skill asks if none is set.
Ask explicitly for a full report on narrow questions.
`--ultra` costs about six research runs; use it for big decisions only.
agents: 5 read-only candidate researchers and 1 verifier (Kongming) with `--ultra`
artifacts: Markdown report at the `Report:` path (usually `plans/reports/`)
Ranking appendix with `--ultra`

ak-research-prompt.tagline: Write a self-contained research brief; does no research itself.
ak-research-prompt.summary: ak:research-prompt writes a brief detailed enough for a human or deep-research AI to deliver sourced, decision-ready results without follow-up questions. Run the brief with `ak:research` or another tool.
howItWorks: Gathers decision, audience, deadline, known facts, and constraints from the conversation and project.
Defines one research question, needed sub-questions, and a primary-sources-first hierarchy.
Requires separating facts, inferences, and uncertainty, plus a gap round and completion threshold.
Returns only the brief, sized to the decision; no research and no second deliverable.
useWhen: Handing work to a deep-research tool or a colleague.
You need strict source and format rules so results are comparable.
You want the question settled before spending research effort.
avoidWhen: You want the research done now: use `ak:research`.
You need a library's docs: use `ak:docs-seeker`.
You need an interview to produce documents: use `ak:interview-docs`.

params.name: <research topic | decision>
params.desc: Topic or decision to inform. No flags.

examples.cmd: /ak:research-prompt "Choose a vector database for RAG over 10 million documents"
/ak:research-prompt "Should we move CI from GitHub Actions to Buildkite"

tips: Keep secrets, internal URLs, and personal data out of briefs sent outside.
One brief per task; split unrelated questions.
Give a deadline and audience to set the completion threshold.
artifacts: Research brief in the conversation; no file.

ak-scout.tagline: Fast, cheap codebase scouting to find the files a task needs.
ak-scout.summary: ak:scout finds relevant files with native search and returns a Scout Report of files, roles, and unresolved questions. Single path or symbol lookups get a direct answer; parallel subagents run only when you ask.
howItWorks: Answers one path or symbol directly with no report.
Sizes the codebase and splits it into non-overlapping scopes.
Spawns parallel Explore subagents only if you ask and the runtime allows; otherwise scouts inline.
`ext` uses OpenCode read-only when local search falls short; agents time out after 3 minutes.
`--ultra` runs five scouts in parallel and a verifier returns a deduped, verified union.
useWhen: Starting a feature that spans several directories.
Finding where feature X lives, or file relationships before debugging.
Before a change that may affect many parts of the codebase.
avoidWhen: You already know which file to read.
Deep semantic analysis: use `ak:gkg` or `ak:graphify`.
Packing the whole repo as context: use `ak:repomix`.

params.name: [search-target]
params.desc: Feature, symbol, path, or task to find. Splits into scopes only when delegation is allowed and useful.

params.name: ext
params.desc: Use permitted OpenCode probes when local search falls short. Read-only; falls back to local search if OpenCode is missing.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: five parallel read-only scouts; verifier returns a deduped, verified union. Fail-closed, no fallback to inline scouting.

examples.cmd: /ak:scout "files related to authentication and sessions"
/ak:scout "payment webhook handler" ext
/ak:scout "the entire data migration flow" --ultra
examples.note: Maximum coverage before a risky change.

tips: Ask explicitly for parallel subagents; otherwise scouting runs inline.
Timed-out scopes are listed; read Unresolved Questions.
`--ultra` needs a runtime that supports five parallel subagents.
agents: 5 read-only candidate scouts and 1 verifier (Kongming) with `--ultra`
artifacts: Markdown Scout Report (Relevant Files, Unresolved Questions)
Scope tracking entries when 3+ agents run

ak-sowat.tagline: Review recent work like a product owner: so what, what next.
ak-sowat.summary: ak:sowat judges recent work, issues, or PRs by user and business outcome, correcting priorities when evidence supports it. It returns up to three next steps with success signals, and never implements, changes issues, or invents data.
howItWorks: Establishes the intended outcome and what was actually implemented, verified, shipped, and still open.
Scores candidates on impact, urgency, confidence, effort, risk, and leverage.
Corrects your priorities directly when evidence supports it, never for show.
Outputs So what, Priority correction, up to three Next steps, and Defer or ignore.
useWhen: You finished a feature and want to know what it means and what's next.
You suspect the team is focused on the wrong thing.
Many open issues need a short priority decision.
avoidWhen: Technical summary of what changed: use `ak:sumup`.
Status of in-flight branches or plans: use `ak:watzup`.
Changing issue states: use `ak:github`.

params.name: [recent-changes|issue|PR]
params.desc: What to analyze. Optional; behavior when omitted is undocumented. No flags.

examples.cmd: /ak:sowat
examples.note: 'So what, what next' from session context.

examples.cmd: /ak:sowat #482

tips: Provide real analytics; the skill never invents adoption or revenue numbers.
It separates implemented, verified, and shipped.
The three-step cap is deliberate.
artifacts: Priority assessment in the conversation; no file or issue changes.

ak-scenario.tagline: Decompose features across 12 dimensions into edge cases and tests.
ak-scenario.summary: ak:scenario breaks a feature or file across 12 dimensions (users, inputs, timing, scale, state, auth, integrity, and more) into severity-ranked edge cases and test targets. It runs one-shot by default, or iteratively with a `scenario-results.tsv` log and composite score.
howItWorks: One-shot: marks applicable dimensions and states the assumption behind each skip.
Generates concrete scenarios tied to invariants and test targets, ranked Critical to Low.
Iterative: one new scenario per iteration, classified New/Variant/Duplicate, logged to `scenario-results.tsv`.
Forces dimension rotation after 3 iterations on one dimension.
Stops after N iterations or 2 with nothing New; ends with a coverage matrix and composite score.
useWhen: Before implementing a complex or stateful feature (payments, OAuth).
Before writing tests, to get prioritized test targets.
Deep coverage audit before a release (`--saturation`).
avoidWhen: One-line fixes, cosmetic tweaks, or config-only changes.
A go/no-go debate on the design: use `ak:predict`.
Running real tests: use `ak:test`.

params.name: <file path or feature description>
params.desc: Required. File to analyze or feature description.

params.name: --iterations N
params.desc: Run exactly N iterations. Without it or `--saturation`, runs one-shot.

params.name: --saturation
params.desc: Iterate until 2 iterations find nothing New; a heuristic, still within the iteration/time budget.

params.name: --domain <type>
params.desc: Dimension priority hint: `software`, `product`, `business`, `security`, `marketing`. Default auto.

params.name: --focus <dim>
params.desc: Prioritize `edge-cases`, `failures`, `security`, or `scale`. Default auto.

params.name: --format <type>
params.desc: `table` (default), `use-cases`, `test-scenarios`, or `threat-scenarios`.

examples.cmd: /ak:scenario src/api/payment.ts
/ak:scenario src/middleware/auth.ts --saturation --domain security
/ak:scenario "Checkout flow" --format test-scenarios

tips: The composite score measures exploration volume, not coverage quality.
`--saturation` can be costly; cap it or use `--iterations N`.
Check skipped dimensions: a wrong skip assumption is a hidden risk.
artifacts: Markdown Scenario Report in the conversation
`scenario-results.tsv` (iterative mode)
